title: Score After Flipping Binary Matrix
description:
You are given an `m x n` binary matrix `grid` containing only `0`s and `1`s.

A **move** consists of choosing any row or any column and toggling every value in that row or column (changing every `0` to `1` and every `1` to `0`).

After performing any number of moves, every row of the matrix is interpreted as a binary number (with column `0` as the most significant bit), and the score of the matrix is the sum of these `m` numbers.

Return the **highest possible score** achievable.
hints: The most significant bit (column 0) outweighs all remaining bits combined, so greedily toggle any row whose first entry is 0 so that column 0 becomes all 1s.
Once row orientations are fixed, maximize each remaining column c independently by counting how many rows have grid[r][c] == grid[r][0] (the effective 1s) and taking max(ones, m - ones).

examples.explanation: Flipping row 0, then column 2, then column 3 produces rows 1111 (15), 1001 (9), and 1111 (15), totaling 39.
Flipping the single 0 to 1 gives a score of 1.
All entries are already 1 in a 2x2 grid (11 + 11 = 3 + 3 = 6), which is optimal.
